title: Ratatouille
subtitle: Slow-cooked Provencal vegetable stew
excerpt: The key to ratatouille that is not a watery mush is cooking the vegetables in stages rather than all at once, and giving the finished pot time to reduce and concentrate. It is better the next day, making it ideal to cook ahead.
sourceNotes: Ratatouille is a Provencal dish from the area around Nice, where the same trio of aubergine, courgette, and peppers appears in various forms across the summer vegetable harvest. The name comes from the French verb touiller, meaning to toss or stir.

recipe.batchNotes: Makes excellent leftovers -- the flavour improves overnight. Serve cold as a side dish or warm through in a pan.

content.text: Salt the aubergine 20 minutes before cooking. This draws out water and helps the pieces brown rather than steam in the pan.
Toss the aubergine cubes with 1 tsp of salt and leave in a colander for 20 minutes. Pat dry with paper towel.

Heat 3 tbsp of olive oil in the saucepan over high heat. Fry the aubergine in two batches until golden on most sides. Remove and set aside. Add the courgette and peppers to the same pan with another tbsp of oil and fry for 4-5 minutes until lightly coloured. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining olive oil to the pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, thyme, and bay leaves and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and 100 ml of water. Simmer for 10 minutes.

Return all the vegetables to the pot, stir gently, and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the vegetables are completely tender. Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the basil off the heat.

items.fix: Fold gently and check the vegetables after 15 minutes. They should hold their shape but feel completely tender.

items.cause: Lid left on during the final simmer.
items.fix: Ensure the pot is uncovered and the heat is high enough to see a gentle bubble across the surface.
